newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-SIX PLAYERS SUSPENDED, FINED FOLLOWING KNICKS-HEAT BRAWL.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-SIX PLAYERS SUSPENDED, FINED FOLLOWING KNICKS-HEAT BRAWL.

text.p: Five New York Knicks players were suspended one game each and P.J. Brown of the Miami Heat was hit with a two-game suspension as the NBA came down hard on offenders in Wednesday night's brawl during the Knicks-Heat playoff game.

Heat forward Brown, who set off the melee near the end of Miami's win over visiting New York by flipping Knicks guard Charlie Ward head over heels after Ward leaned low against him to box out for a rebound, was fined $10,000.
Knicks players Ward, Patrick Ewing, Allan Houston, Larry Johnson and John Starks all were suspended one game and fined. Ward will be docked $6,000 and the others were fined $2,500.
Ewing, Houston, Johnson and Starks were suspended for leaving the bench during an altercation.

Because NBA rules require a team to have at least nine players dressed and available to play for a playoff game, the league decided the suspensions of Ewing, Houston, Johnson and Starks would be split between two games and served in alphabetical order.

Ewing and Houston, along with Ward, will sit out Game 6 at Madison Square Garden Friday. Johnson and Starks must sit out either Game 7 of the Eastern Conference semifinals against Miami or Game 1 of the Eastern Conference finals, should the Knicks advance Friday to a series against the Chicago Bulls.
The penalties were announced by NBA senior vice president Rod Thorn.
Wednesday's game in Miami, in which the Heat staved off elimination with a 96-81 win, was marred by four ejections and an ugly melee in the final two minutes.
The Knicks lead the best-of-seven series 3-2 with Game 6 here on Friday.
Brown, Ward and John Starks were ejected following the brawl. Shortly before the scuffle, New York forward Charles Oakley was ejected for shoving Heat centre Alonzo Mourning.
Along with the suspension and individual fines, the Knicks organisation was fined $20,000 -- $5,000 for each player who left the bench area.
Starks was also fined an additional $5,000 for making an obscene gesture towards the crowd following the incident, which occurred with 1:53 remaining.
